newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary bourse says futures turnover rises sharply.
newsitem.headline: Hungary bourse says futures turnover rises sharply.

text.p: Futures turnover on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) has risen sharply this year, BSE Managing Director Jozsef Rotyis said on Thursday.
Rotyis told a news conference that turnover in futures deals on the BSE was 47 percent of the Budapest Commodity Exchange's (BCE) total in May, compared with 10 percent in the whole of 1996.
He did not disclose the May turnover figures.
BSE's futures turnover was boosted mainly by deals in BUX index futures, a product which the BCE does not have, while on the BCE most of the futures turnover is generated in currency deals.
A National Bank of Hungary (NBH) move to allow foreigners trading in futures would increase the BSE's futures turnover substantially, Rotyis said.

"Some 50 to 60 percent of the (BSE's) spot share turnover is generated by foreigners," he said. "If they are allowed to enter the futures market, a (turnover) increase of at least this percentage is likely there."
On the BSE's futures market foreign investors can trade only for the BUX index.

A central bank official said earlier the board of the NBH was likely to consider the liberalisation of cross-border capital flows at the end of June and a decision on freeing futures markets may come.
